historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly flags a state change but treats a source example as a universally executable value and changes transport without an equivalence decision.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly prevents blind use of 0x00 0x46, adds physical effect monitoring and makes restoration mandatory.
historical_reviews.history: The invalidated earlier-run artifact was located but excluded as authority; the paired getter remains separately reviewed and supplies no write permission.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A power-control write requires explicit target/value approval, hard aborts and recovery even when the raw bytes appear in the source.

original_test_intent: Apply one owner-approved CPU-domain power cap, verify the exact value through the paired getter and observe bounded power, temperature and throttling behavior before restoring the original policy.
original_method: Retain in-band 0x30/0x27 plus 0x30/0x26 read-back, but do not execute the sample payload until the private encoding and platform-safe cap range are approved.
manual_activity: The power/thermal owner identifies the capped CPU/socket/package domain, approves a value within the platform range, confirms workload conditions and dwell, defines abort thresholds and authorizes restoration to the captured baseline.
required_inputs: Cap byte order, scale, units and allowed range
Vendor proof for the 0x00 0x46 to 150 W example if used
Current cap and full power/thermal/workload baseline
Approved test cap, dwell and stabilization time
Power, temperature, throttling and workload abort limits
Exact baseline restore value and recovery path
safety_requirements: Do not assume the example is safe or universally encoded
Never set zero, below-minimum or above-platform cap
Continuously monitor package/system power and critical temperatures
Abort on instability or ambiguous read-back
Restore the original cap on every exit path
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, contract, cap domain and safe range
Read and archive the original cap plus power/thermal/workload baseline
Display exact write bytes and decoded value for explicit OK
Abort and restore on any unsafe response
Restore the captured cap and confirm stabilized post-state
Archive command, telemetry and no-unapproved-mutation evidence
engineer_actions: Approve encoding, domain, value, duration and workload
Approve measurable abort thresholds and recovery
Resolve whether OOB may substitute for the source's in-band path

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The example command is syntactically complete, but neither the private 0x0046-to-150 W mapping nor its platform safety is established; switching to OOB also requires an explicit equivalence contract.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Read the baseline with approved 0x30 0x26, encode one owner-approved cap under the vendor contract, issue raw 0x30 0x27 <exact-cap-bytes> once, verify read-back and bounded telemetry, then restore the original bytes.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source's 0x00 0x46 example, read-back step and 10/5 timing are preserved as evidence; none is treated as an approved universal operating value.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the cap change as a reversible control experiment with a captured baseline, byte-to-watt proof, one bounded mutation, live power/thermal/throttling interlocks and verified restoration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds domain and encoding validation, rejects command-success-only acceptance, and requires physical effect plus recovery evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-back proves configured state but not enforcement; telemetry without exact write/read-back cannot prove the OEM setter changed the intended policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An overly low cap can destabilize timing-sensitive workloads and an excessive or misdecoded cap can violate electrical/thermal policy; competing firmware may overwrite the value asynchronously.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish or vendor power-control API may substitute only with documented mapping to the same cap domain/value and restoration behavior; otherwise it is separate coverage and raw 0x30/0x27 remains untested.
expected_evidence: Original cap raw bytes plus decoded value and complete baseline
Exact set request/response, completion, transport and timing
Restored cap raw/decoded evidence and stable post-state
Preserved BMC/OS/SEL logs and no-unapproved-mutation audit

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master consistently describes an in-band cap write followed by getter read-back. Its 150 W example is under-specified and cannot be interpreted safely without the vendor encoding, but no Master field directly supplies a contradictory command or acceptance target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The setter, read-back and reversible control purpose are identifiable. Vendor encoding, platform limits, an approved value and recovery are explicit package/user inputs, so the review is not irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Prevents a sample payload from becoming an unsafe default and turns a completion-only policy write into a closed-loop, domain-qualified power-control test with mandatory rollback.
independent_technical_reasoning: A raw cap is an actuator setting whose meaning depends on private encoding and CPU power domain. The literal two-byte value 0x0046 does not independently establish 150 W, so the label must be proven by the vendor contract rather than arithmetic assumption. Read-back alone is still insufficient: monitored power, temperature, throttling and workload stability are required to show the approved cap behaves safely before restoration.
